intro.text: The Inca Trail is a hiking route in Peru that ends at Machu Picchu; the Classic route starts at Km 82, Piscacucho, beside the Urubamba River.
Along the way it crosses cloud forest and alpine tundra, passes Inca ruins and tunnels, and climbs above 4,200 metres.
The trail is part of the Qhapaq Ñan, the Inca road system listed by UNESCO in 2014. Daily numbers are capped, and every trekker must walk with a guide.
The Tour du Mont Blanc is a long-distance hiking loop around the Mont Blanc massif, normally walked anticlockwise from Les Houches through France, Italy and Switzerland.
It crosses seven valleys, among them the Chamonix valley, the Vallée des Glaciers, Italy's Val Veny and Val Ferret, and the Swiss Val Ferret.
In 1767 the Genevan scientist Horace-Bénédict de Saussure completed his first tour of Mont Blanc, a journey that helped reveal the topography of the Savoy Alps.
The W Trek traces a W-shaped route of about 70 km through Torres del Paine National Park in Chilean Patagonia.
It passes lenga forests, rivers and glaciers, skirts Lake Nordenskjöld beneath the Cuernos del Paine, and offers views of Grey Glacier.
The park was established in 1959 and named a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1978; 'Paine' means 'blue' in the Tehuelche (Aonikenk) language.
The trek starts and ends at Lukla and takes about two weeks, following the Dudh Koshi valley, lined with tea houses, towards Mount Everest.
Past Monjo, walkers enter Sagarmatha National Park, which includes Everest and in 1979 became Nepal's first national park inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site.
Beyond Lobuche, on the lateral moraine of the Khumbu Glacier, Gorak Shep is the last settlement before the Kala Patthar viewpoint and base camp.
The Milford Track runs 53.5 km through Fiordland National Park, from Glade Wharf at the head of Lake Te Anau to Sandfly Point on Milford Sound.
Walkers follow the Clinton and Arthur valleys over four days, in one direction only, staying at Clinton, Mintaro and Dumpling huts.
In 1888 Quintin McKinnon found the pass now named after him, and he became the first guide to take walkers from Lake Te Anau to Milford Sound.
The crossing begins at 1,120 m on a boardwalk in the Mangatepōpō Valley and ends at Ketetahi Road, 760 m, after a long zig-zag descent of the northern slopes.
Until 2007 it was called the Tongariro Crossing; 'Alpine' was added to emphasise the extreme weather on the exposed terrain.
The mountains are sacred to Ngāti Hikairo ki Tongariro of Ngāti Tūwharetoa, and in 1993 Tongariro became the first property inscribed under World Heritage cultural landscape criteria.
The Nakahechi is the main route linking the three Grand Shrines of Kumano; this walk covers it from Takijiri-oji, beside the Tonda River, to Kumano Hongu Taisha.
Most walkers split the roughly 37 km of mountain trail into two days, stopping in the village of Chikatsuyu about halfway.
People from peasants to emperors walked to Kumano, and retired emperors made repeated pilgrimages there in the 11th and 12th centuries.
The Laugavegur is a hiking trail in southern Iceland, usually walked north to south over four days from Landmannalaugar to the glacial valley of Þórsmörk.
It is known for its varied landscapes: colourful mountains, black lava, bubbling hot springs, lakes, canyons and a black sandy desert.
The trail was established in 1978 and is maintained by Ferðafélag Íslands, which runs the mountain huts at each stage.
The West Highland Way runs 154 km (96 miles) from Milngavie, north of Glasgow, to Fort William, and is usually walked south to north from the Lowlands into the Highlands.
It follows the shore of Loch Lomond, crosses the open wilderness of Rannoch Moor and passes Glen Coe before reaching Fort William at the foot of Ben Nevis.
Lord Mansfield opened the route on 6 October 1980. It is now one of Scotland's Great Trails, and that programme's website calls it the country's most popular long-distance route.
The Camino Francés, or French Way, runs from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port on the French side of the Pyrenees to Santiago de Compostela in Galicia.
On its way west it crosses Navarre, La Rioja, Castile and León and Galicia, passing through cities such as Pamplona, Burgos and León.
The route was described in 1135 in the Codex Calixtinus, a medieval pilgrims' guide attributed to the French cleric Aymeric Picaud.
The gorge lies on the Jinsha River, a primary tributary of the upper Yangtze, about 60 km north of Lijiang in Yunnan.
The high trail climbs from Qiaotou up the 28 Bends switchbacks to Halfway Guesthouse, then descends to Tina's on the road.
Legend says the gorge is named after a hunted tiger that escaped by leaping across the river at its narrowest point.
The Half Dome day hike starts at Happy Isles and climbs past Vernal and Nevada falls into Little Yosemite Valley before turning toward the dome.
The round trip is 14 to 16 miles with about 4,800 feet of climbing, and most hikers take 10 to 12 hours.
An 1865 report called the summit 'perfectly inaccessible'; George Anderson reached it in October 1875, and cables were first built near his route in 1919.
